anatomy.note: This site's picture of where the kinds of firm on this page are heading. It is a model of an idea, joined from the arguments on the page before; no reading tests it whole.

parts.does: Set the task, sign the work, hold the licence, face the customer, and pay when it is wrong. Few, senior, and named.
parts.name: The people who answer

parts.does: Tests, reviewers and records that settle whether work was done right. Where no check exists, a person's judgement stands in, and this is where most work waits.
parts.name: The checking layer

parts.does: Agents now; agents that keep context next; robots later. Wide, cheap, and not employed.
parts.name: The working base

parts.does: The models themselves, bought by the unit of text processed and, in this site's view, from whoever sells them cheapest.
parts.name: Rented

parts.does: What cannot be bought: customers, the firm's records and context, its licences, its sensors and sites.
parts.name: Owned

anatomy.title: The anatomy of an AI-run firm

kinds.later: Little changes with robots: the work is on screens, apart from stock counts and site visits.
kinds.name: Accounting practice
kinds.next: A client's books are years of context, so an agent that keeps it does the preparation and the first review. The practice becomes reviewers and client partners, with few preparers and few trainees.
kinds.now: Buyers built around AI own these firms more than sell to them, and this site lists more such buyers here than in any other trade. An owner of many such firms reports a tax trial that cut preparation time; its chief said the year before that the aim was not to replace accountants and that he did not expect AI to end the need for them. A bookkeeping firm says its software runs the books from sign-up to the monthly close with no person involved and logs every decision. Every figure is the operators' own.
kinds.signs: A licensed accountant for audits and reviews only; tax returns and bookkeeping need no licensed signature
titles: Accounting, Tax Preparation, Bookkeeping, and Payroll Services
kinds.wrong: A buyer of such firms reporting, after a full tax season, revenue per person no higher than ordinary firms; or a state board disciplining a firm over audit work an agent prepared.

kinds.later: Robots do not bear on it.
kinds.name: Law firm
kinds.next: A firm's precedents and each client's history are held by the agent. The ratio of junior lawyers to partners turns over: fewer associates under each partner, and more matters for each lawyer who signs.
kinds.now: The census passes none of the work in a lawyer's own role, mostly because no check that exists today settles it. A researcher's running list holds a great many court decisions in which a filing relied on material AI had made up; more of those filings came from people acting without a lawyer than from lawyers. A new firm says its agents research and draft while its lawyers review all of the work; that is the firm's own account. The regulator for England and Wales has authorised a firm run on AI for small debt claims, on conditions: it may not propose case law, it acts only on a step the client has approved, and named solicitors answer for the output.
kinds.signs: A named lawyer on every piece of work; outside a few places, only lawyers may own the firm
kinds.wrong: A large firm publishing steady hiring of junior lawyers after years of agent use; or firms owned by non-lawyers failing to grow where they are allowed.

kinds.later: Robots matter only for work in the field, such as fitting equipment.
kinds.name: Software and IT services company
kinds.next: Agents hold the whole body of a company's code and its history. Engineers specify, review and answer; managers who relayed information thin out; the junior rung is the open question.
kinds.now: By adoption this is the trade furthest along. This site's reading is that tests give it a check most engineers accept, though the census passes less of its payroll than it does in accounting. A large company said in 2024 that AI wrote a sizeable share of its new code, which engineers then reviewed. A randomised trial with the tools of early 2025 found experienced developers slower with AI while believing themselves faster. The same group's repeat with later tools pointed the other way, towards a speed-up, and its authors call that result unreliable because many developers would no longer work without AI. Among the large Indian outsourcers the counts are mixed: the biggest employs fewer people than a year before, another employs more, and the reporting cites weak demand as well as AI.
kinds.signs: The engineer who reviews and accepts the change; no licence
titles: Computer Systems Design and Related Services
kinds.wrong: A sound repeat of the trial, with developers who cannot opt out, still finding a slowdown; or the outsourcers' headcount recovering as demand does.

kinds.later: Branches and cash are the only physical part.
kinds.name: Bank or lender
kinds.next: An agent that remembers the customer handles most service and processing. People sit in risk, exceptions and the decisions an examiner will ask about.
kinds.now: What is on record here is in service and operations; this site found nothing on agents deciding who gets credit. A bank's consumer chief projected fewer people in operations and account services, with no date. A payments lender that froze hiring and leaned on a chatbot said quality fell and began hiring service staff again. A bank that declared service jobs redundant in favour of a voice bot called it an error and reversed it. In April 2026 the American bank regulators reissued their guidance on managing models, put generative and agentic AI outside its scope, and said they would ask for views on AI later. This site reads that as leaving a bank with no agreed template for showing a regulator's examiner that an agent is under control.
titles: Credit Intermediation and Related Activities (5221 and 5223 only)
kinds.wrong: The regulators bringing agents under the model guidance unchanged; or the bank that projected fewer operations staff reporting no fall.

kinds.later: Robots or drones inspect damage; repair stays with other trades.
kinds.name: Insurer or insurance broker
kinds.next: Software takes in a claim, checks it and pays it. People remain for refusals, disputes and large or strange risks, and for selling to businesses.
kinds.now: An insurer built on AI reports premiums, the payments its customers make for cover, growing far faster than its staff and says rivals spend far more than it does on handling claims, by its own estimate of the industry; it still loses money. A bill introduced in New Jersey would leave sorting, fraud scoring and approvals to software and bar software from making the final refusal, for home, motor and flood cover only; it has not reached a committee. A wider bill in Florida, which would have required a qualified person to make every refusal, died in March 2026. On brokers this site found almost nothing.
kinds.signs: A licensed adjuster or seller, under licensing rules this page did not read; under a bill now proposed, a person for the final refusal of some claims
titles: Agencies, Brokerages, and Other Insurance Related Activities
kinds.wrong: That insurer's staff growing in step with its premiums; or the New Jersey bill dying as Florida's did, leaving no state that requires a person for a refusal.

kinds.later: This is where robots would matter most and are furthest off: bodies are fragile, and much of a clinician's work needs hands, which the census sets aside as physical.
kinds.name: Hospital or medical practice
kinds.next: An agent holding the patient's whole record drafts, orders and follows up routine care. Clinicians examine, decide and sign, each for more patients; the office behind them thins.
kinds.now: The use on record is note-taking: software that writes up the visit. In a study with no comparison group, whose authors include staff of the software's maker, fewer clinicians reported burnout after a month of use. An independent institute's report, drawn from interviews with early users, calls the financial effect unclear. Utah has waived its licensing law to let a company's software renew routine prescriptions without a doctor signing, once doctors have reviewed its early decisions for each class of drug; the company says its malpractice insurance covers the software. Members of the state's medical licensing board asked for a halt in April 2026. The state declined, saying doctors were still reviewing every renewal in the opening phase.
kinds.signs: A licensed clinician, everywhere but one state's trial
kinds.wrong: Harm in that state's trial, or other states copying it quickly; or a controlled trial finding note-taking software does nothing for burnout.

kinds.later: Robots do not bear on it: the work is done on screens and telephones.
kinds.name: Customer-support and business-support firm
kinds.next: An agent that remembers each customer and learns from corrections takes first contact. The firm sells results, not seats, and keeps a small team for the cases that escalate.
kinds.now: The trade with the most figures and the most reversals, nearly all of them about customer support. A software company that sells AI agents says it now runs its own support with far fewer people. A large contact-centre operator reports revenue slightly down on a year before; the largest by headcount expects little or no growth. The best-measured study this site found, of an AI assistant working beside support staff inside a company, found the staff faster, novices most. A payments firm that leaned on a chatbot says quality fell and is hiring support staff again. Staffing agencies, a neighbouring trade this page does not draw, have a target from a large agency and little else.
kinds.signs: Nobody by law; the customer who expects a person
kinds.wrong: The large operators' revenue recovering; or the software company that cut its support staff reporting that it has hired them back.

kinds.later: Robots do not bear on it.
kinds.name: Management consultancy
kinds.next: Research, analysis and drafts come from agents that hold the firm's past work. Fewer, more senior people sell, frame the question and stand behind the answer.
kinds.now: The evidence is thin and mostly second-hand. What is on record is a failure: a large firm agreed to repay part of a government fee after its report was found to quote a court judgment and cite research papers that did not exist; the department said the report's recommendations stood. This site's reading is that there is no licence and no accepted check for advice, so the client cannot verify it and reputation carries the sale.
kinds.signs: A partner, on the firm's name alone
titles: Management, Scientific, and Technical Consulting Services
kinds.wrong: A leading firm publishing its headcount by level and showing junior intake holding steady.

kinds.later: Of the service trades this is the one robots would change most, through maintenance; this site found no evidence of it yet.
kinds.name: Property manager or letting agency
kinds.next: Software that knows each building and tenant runs the tenancy. People win landlords, handle disputes and hold the client money.
kinds.now: The clearest case of a buyer of firms. A British buyer of letting agencies says each of its property managers handles a multiple of the usual number of homes, with software handling messages, rent, compliance and the arranging of repairs. Its investor says profit margins rose sharply at agencies where the software is fully in use. The count is the company's own and the margin claim its investor's; neither has been independently checked. This site found no account of software or robots doing the repairs or viewings themselves.
kinds.signs: In England, the agent who holds clients' money; licensing elsewhere varies and was not read for this page
kinds.wrong: An independent count putting that buyer's homes per person near the ordinary level; or complaints rising at the agencies it bought.

kinds.later: In this site's view the trade robots reach first: fixed routes and warehouses now, general handling later. The yard and the road are where the firm changes most.
kinds.name: Freight and logistics operator
kinds.next: Quoting, booking and tracking run without people. The broker's office becomes a small desk for exceptions and customers.
kinds.now: Most of the payroll here is in driving and warehouse jobs, which the census does not score. In the office part, a large American freight broker reports each person handling markedly more shipments a day than at the end of 2022; it is a company measure, and the report does not separate what AI did from anything else. A company running driverless trucks says they are hauling freight on fixed routes and that it plans many more by the end of 2026. A retailer says it has put a very large number of mobile robots into its warehouses; they are not humanoids, meaning robots shaped like a person.
kinds.signs: A registered broker or carrier, under rules this page did not read
kinds.wrong: The broker's gain reversing when freight volumes recover; or the driverless operator missing its fleet target.

kinds.later: The kind of firm most exposed to robots and least sure of the date. One carmaker plans humanoids on a line within a few years; a veteran roboticist, who sells robots of another kind, expects robot hands to stay far short of human ones beyond 2036.
kinds.name: Manufacturer
kinds.next: Planning, purchasing and scheduling are run by agents that know the plant. Engineers and managers remain; clerical work thins.
kinds.now: This site found almost nothing on agents in a manufacturer's offices, and says so. On the floor the base is ordinary industrial robots, installed in large numbers every year by the count of the robot makers' own federation. The humanoid trial with the most published detail is its maker's own account of a loading task at a car plant, and no other task; it ran for most of a year and ended when the maker retired that generation of robot for its successor.
kinds.signs: Whoever answers for product safety and for the workers beside the machines
kinds.wrong: A carmaker publishing a humanoid's cost per task below a worker's; or the dated plan slipping.

kinds.later: Warehouses first, as in freight. The shop floor changes last, because shoppers are there.
kinds.name: Retailer
kinds.next: Agents buy, price and plan stock within limits a person sets. Head office thins; the shop floor does not.
kinds.now: The world's largest private employer, a retailer, says it expects its headcount to stay flat for some years while the jobs change. In its maker's own test, an AI model set to run a small office shop lost money and told customers to pay into an account it had made up. In a later round with more tools and another AI overseeing it, the maker reports the shop began to make money, though staff could still talk it into bad deals. Checkout without cashiers was taken out of a grocery chain's larger stores and kept in its smaller ones and for other retailers. Shelf-scanning robots were dropped by a large retailer in 2020, before the current models.
kinds.signs: The store operator; pharmacy and alcohol aside, no licence
titles: Food and Beverage Retailers (4451 and 4452 only)
kinds.wrong: That retailer's headcount falling well before the decade ends; or an AI running a shop at a profit with no person or other AI correcting it, as reported by someone other than its maker.

stages.name: Now
stages.rests_on: What operators and regulators have published, and this site's census. Most operator figures are their own.

stages.name: Next
stages.rests_on: Judgement. Today's models do not change from what they do on the job. A widely read interviewer of AI researchers put even odds on models learning on the job as a person does by 2032. A recent preprint, not yet peer reviewed, shows a memory kept outside the model helping on a banking test.
stages.what: Agents that keep context and learn on the job

stages.name: Later
stages.rests_on: Extrapolation. The evidence is a few trials and plans. A bank's forecast puts the real rise late in the next decade, and another bank's runs only to its middle. A veteran roboticist expects robot hands to stay far short of human ones beyond 2036.
stages.what: Robots that do physical work with that context
